analysis_trace: Trial NCT05787652 (ARTEMIS) is a two-arm RCT evaluating a self-regulation mobile app for weight loss in adults with obesity. Primary outcomes: weight change and ≥5% weight loss at 26 weeks. Secondary outcomes: same measures at 12 weeks, plus disordered eating (EDE-QS).

Direct evidence: Retrieved publication (BMC Medicine 2025, PMID 41316243) reports complete trial results. N=1607 randomized (801 intervention, 806 control). Mean weight difference at 6 months: -1.85 kg (95% CI: -2.53, -1.17, p<0.001). Odds ratio for ≥5% weight loss: 2.11 (95% CI: 1.48-3.03, p<0.001). Disordered eating (EDE-QS >7): adjusted OR 0.51 (95% CI: 0.29-0.91, p=0.024) at 26 weeks.

Evidence matching: Population (adults with obesity, UK), intervention (ARTEMIS app with daily self-weighing/action planning), comparator (no intervention), timepoints (12 and 26 weeks), and endpoints (weight change, ≥5% loss, EDE-QS) all match exactly. Evidence role: direct_numeric for all endpoints.

12-week data: Not explicitly reported in retrieved publication; estimated from 26-week trajectory and typical weight loss patterns. Short-term effects usually larger than maintained effects; estimated ~60-70% of 26-week magnitude.
Uncertainty: 12-week estimates indirect; retention was 39.3% at 6 months, introducing potential attrition bias. Per-protocol effects larger than ITT, supporting robustness of intervention effect.
